title: Treasury Marketable Borrowing Estimates (Q1 2027 / Q2 2027), 15:00 ET
source: EST: canonical file written by this event's own never-assessed initial research (2026-09-10), reading the one proposal that named it (proposals/treasury-borrowing-estimates-2027-02-01.from-sloos-2027-02-01.json). THE DATE IS UNCHANGED AT 2027-02-01 AND ITS DERIVATION IS NOW MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSERTED. The proposal derived it from the pairing the two existing borrowing-estimates entries document (estimates Monday = refunding Wednesday minus two sessions) plus this calendar's already-tracked treasury-refunding-2027-02-03. Both halves were re-derived from scratch here against api.fiscaldata.treasury.gov/services/api/fiscal_service/v1/accounting/od/auctions_query, fetched direct 2026-09-10 (HTTP 200), whose announcemt_date on the Feb/May/Aug/Nov 30-Year NEW ISSUE (original_issue_date null, i.e. not a reopening) IS the quarterly refunding announcement: 51 cycles, 2014-02 through 2026-08, three more than the sibling treasury-borrowing-estimates-2027-05-03 audited. The window rule holds 51 of 51 — the announcement is the single Wednesday inside [the 30th of the prior month .. the 6th of the refunding month]. FEBRUARY 2027 OPENS ON A MONDAY, the class in which that window contains exactly one Wednesday and no tie-break is needed: 7 of 7 in the record, every one landing on day 3. So the announcement is Wednesday 2027-02-03 and the estimates release is the Monday two sessions earlier, 2027-02-01. ONE CORRECTION TO THE SIBLING, from the three extra cycles: its Friday-1st tie-break ('May takes the later Wednesday, February/August/November the earlier') is 7 of 8, not 8 of 8 — 2014-08 is an August that took the LATER Wednesday (2014-08-06, with 2014-07-30 also in window). That does not touch February 2027, which needs no tie-break, but any lane deriving a Friday-1st refunding date should treat the tie-break as a 7-of-8 heuristic rather than a rule. STAYS estimate: home.treasury.gov/policy-issues/financing-the-government/quarterly-refunding/most-recent-quarterly-refunding-documents, re-fetched direct 2026-09-10 (HTTP 200, 73,660 bytes), publishes exactly one cycle ahead — it reads '(The next release is scheduled for November 2, 2026)' under Financing Estimates, '(The next release is scheduled for November 4 , 2026)' under the refunding statement and '(The next release is scheduled for October 16, 2026)' for the primary-dealer agenda, and names no 2027 date at all — and a rule-derived date is never self-confirmed by this lane. Promotion to TSY:/confirmed is expected at the 2026-11-02/11-04 cycle, which by this series' own convention names its successor
notes: The QUANTITY half of February-2027 refunding week: the 15:00 ET Monday release carries the Jan-Mar 2027 borrowing number and its revision against the figure set on 2026-11-02, the assumed end-March cash balance, and the FIRST estimate for Apr-Jun 2027; treasury-refunding-2027-02-03 (est) allocates it across the curve 48 hours later. Impact LOW, and this session re-measured rather than inherited it: across 51 releases 2014-02 to 2026-08 (dates rebuilt from the auction API, FOMC dates rebuilt from federalreserve.gov's own current and historical calendars), the 26 releases since 2015 that were not FOMC meeting-eves closed TLT 11/26 up at -0.005% (permutation p=0.977), IEF +0.006% (p=0.942), ^TNX +0.041% (p=0.910) — the sibling's figures reproduced to three decimals from an independently rebuilt FOMC set — and adding the four pre-2015 clean releases leaves TLT at +0.029% (p=0.862, n=29). 2027-02-01 is NOT an FOMC eve: the Fed's published 2027 calendar (federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm, fetched direct 2026-09-10) has Jan 26-27 and then Mar 16-17, so the January decision falls five days BEFORE this release and the only significant effect in the whole study — the eve-subset T+1/T+2 bond bid, TLT +0.436% p=0.029 on n=21 — structurally cannot fire. TWO THINGS ARE THIS EDITION'S OWN. (1) It is a better candidate than the May edition to be the FIRST DEBT-LIMIT-LIVE borrowing estimate, because Jan-Mar 2027 is the quarter the arithmetic exhausts: debt outstanding was $40.0743T on 2026-09-09 against the $41.1T ceiling ($1.0257T of headroom), and at the trailing-12m pace (+$650B/qtr) headroom is gone about 2027-01-31 while the last-two-full-quarters pace (+$474B/qtr) puts it about 2027-03-25 — both inside the quarter this release reports on. (2) It CORRECTS the sibling's registered equity drift rather than inheriting it. Every release Monday is a Monday by construction, so the sibling's control (the 120 first-business-days that were not release days, SPY +0.092%) mixes weekdays. Against the weekday-matched control — the 33 first-business-day MONDAYS that were not releases, SPY +0.266% — the 17 clean first-business-day releases at +0.478% are indistinguishable (Welch t = 0.78), while first-business-day NON-Mondays run +0.026% (n=87) even though ISM Manufacturing prints on those mornings too. So neither the Treasury release nor ISM owns the drift, and it does not survive the window: on full SPY history first-business-day Mondays are +0.156% (p=0.140, n=155) while first-business-day non-Mondays are +0.259% (p=0.003, n=249) — the ranking reverses. 2027-02-01 is itself a first-business-day Monday. READ IT, DO NOT TRADE IT. Attribution on the day is impossible in any case: BoJ Summary of Opinions, ISM Manufacturing (10:00 ET, high), SLOOS (14:00 ET) and this release (15:00 ET) share the session, the FOMC decided 01-27, the refunding lands 02-03 and payrolls 02-05. Proposed 2026-09-09 during the never-assessed initial research of sloos-2027-02-01; canonical file written 2026-09-10 by this event's own initial research.
